messages:
Alex G: taking handoff now — I'm primary for the overnight window. Quick summary: active alert INC-2026-53 (rate-engine p99 latency spike, us-west) is still open. See alert link: https://redwood/integrations/pager/INC-2026-53 :rotating_light:
Tara N: thanks. i'm secondary. current baseline p99 usually ~220ms? what's it at now?
Alex G: p99 is ~3.4s for text-generation routes hitting rate-engine-prod-usw. Errors are low (500s <0.5%) but latency is degrading under tail. A few customers reported slow responses.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-53 created by SRE Pager — rule: rate-engine-p99-gt-2s-usw — started 2026-03-14T23:12:11Z.
Mike S: putting short note here — i spun up an emergency replica earlier (scale to 8 -> 12) and warmed caches. That reduced average but tail still rough.
Alex G: actions in flight:
- scaled rate-engine-prod-usw to 12 replicas (`kubectl scale deployment rate-engine -n prod-usw --replicas=12`).
- enabled fallback-model variant (rate-engine-quant-small) for premium-less routes via routing policy for 10m.
- increased prefix cache TTL to 60s for common prefixes.
Linh V: are there ongoing OOMs or GC pauses? logs looked OK when I checked.
Mike S: no OOMs. saw a few 10-20ms GC spikes on two nodes but nothing at crash level.
Alex G: main hypothesis: some clients sending long sequences causing kv-cache churn + kernel selection causing longer per-token time at p99. Also a small subset of tenants hitting heavy parallelism.
Tara N: customer impact: which tenants? any major enterprise?
Alex G: two tenants (acme-labs, quickdocs) saw elevated tail; both are non-SLA trial customers. No sign of org-wide impact. Still, we want to keep p99 <1s.
SRE Pager: paging policy note — if p99 > 5s or error rate >1% escalate to oncall+eng-runtime.
Alex G: runbook pointers: https://redwood/runbooks/rate-engine-latency and playbook snippet below:
```
1) Check `kubectl get pods -n prod-usw -l app=rate-engine` for restart/oom
2) Inspect /var/log/rate-engine/*.log for full-queue/backpressure lines
3) Toggle fallback routing: curl -X POST https://admin/routing/override -d '{"route":"text.gen","variant":"quant-small","duration":600}'
4) If tail persists, add replicas in increments of 2, monitor p99 for 5m
```
Mike S: i left detailed cmds in the bridge notes. if someone needs them i can paste.
Alex G: current mitigations status: scaled=done, fallback=enabled (monitoring), cache-ttl=done. Observability: traced two slow requests — attached stack traces show repeated attention kernel fallback on node gpu-17.
Tara N: can we reroute traffic away from gpu-17?
Alex G: yes — routing control available. I'll cordon that node and let k8s reschedule. Command: `kubectl cordon gpu-17 && kubectl drain gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — will do after 2 more minutes of monitoring.
Linh V: if we drain, we should pre-warm other nodes with model cache. I'll run the prefetch script: `./tools/prefetch --model rate-v2 --nodes 3 --region us-west`.
Alex G: doing drain now — executing: `kubectl cordon gpu-17`
Alex G: drain started. re-scheduling in progress.
SRE Pager: automated note — scaling event detected, autoscaler paused for manual scale (reason: manual override).
Mike S: after cordon, i see pods landing on gpu-21 and gpu-22. prefetch successful on gpu-21. p99 dropping to ~1.1s.
Tara N: good. still above target but trending down. Any outstanding customer messages?
Alex G: sent status update to support for affected orgs: short message: "We're investigating higher latencies in us-west; temporary mitigations applied, no data loss, updates forthcoming."
Tara N: coverage notes for handoff: I'm oncall through 06:00 PDT. Alex, can you keep primary until 01:30 and then pass to me? Also, Linh is covering EU1 so tag her if any cross-region issues.
Alex G: yes — I'll stay until 01:30 and do full handoff. Current TODOs for next shift:
- watch p99 for 30m, if rises above 2s re-enable broader fallback for all non-paying routes
- validate cache-hardening didn't regress quality (check top-25 prompt logs)
- confirm node cordon didn't create eviction cascade
Mike S: I'll keep a lightweight watch on k8s events and post any cluster-level anomalies to this thread.
Linh V: FYI, EU1 seems fine. prefetch script also ran in eu1 as precaution.
Alex G: incident note for postmortem: capture kernel-selection pattern on gpu-17 and whether specific request shapes cause fallback. Also include cost delta from emergency scale.
Tara N: handover checklist to me at 01:30: attach alert graph links, current replica count, active overrides, list of affected customers, and whether fallback is still enabled.
Alex G: will post final snapshot at 01:28. Also tagging @oncall-bot to summarize runbook actions at shift change.
oncall-bot: reminder set for 01:28 to post handoff snapshot.
Mike S: minor nit — the fallback routing API logs show one 403 earlier (token expired). I rotated the token and left note in ops-keys. Not blocking.
Tara N: cool. coverage gap note: between 02:00-03:00 PDT there is low coverage in APAC team; if anything cross-regional pops up we should escalate to eng-runtime.
Alex G: noted. will highlight that in the handoff message.
Linh V: i'm around if APAC needs help; i can bridge if needed.
Alex G: final: current state = mitigations holding, p99 ~1.0-1.2s and trending down, no raised customer SLAs impacted. will post snapshot at 01:28 and transfer primary to Tara at 01:30 per plan.
Tara N: thanks — i'll take over then. please DM if anything spikes. :thumbsup:
